Content: First of all, I want to be clear on what seems to be confusing to a lot of people: just because you buy some scrubs, a stethoscope, and possibly work in a clinic or office does not equal “a nurse”. There’s no way this girl is a real “nurse”. A registered nurse has at a minimum a college degree and in many cases, more than one. It’s a vigorous path that requires tons of hours of classes, clinicals, and not to mention state and federal background checks. If you obtain your DEGREE and manage to pass rigorous clinical training above and beyond a regular degree, then you may qualify to take the Registered Nurse State Board Exam. It is not an easy exam to pass by any means. If you pass that exam, only then can you achieve the title of Registered Nurse and receive a license from your state. You also must Swear an oath just like a physician to never bring or cause harm to any person. I highly doubt this person is a Nurse. Content: STOP IT! If she’s only 19 there’s no way she can be a nurse. I suspect she’s actually a nurses aide of some sort. It infuriates me when public platforms put all health care workers in the same pot. As far as nursing, there are three categories. A four year degreed RN, an associate degree RN ( which still holds the same job and responsibilities. And many are just awesome!). The only difference between these degrees is that the four year has taken additional classes in management etc.). And finally LPN, which I believe is a two year certificate. They are restricted in what they can do, like hanging IV meds, but many can get additional training to get a certificate in order to do this. I personally have a four year degree, but I’ve worked with many amazing and super smart people who have associate degrees and LPN’s. Content:
She's a kid. To all of the armchair psychologist,  you can't diagnose the girl off a couple of TikTok video's.  Less than 2 minutes of her life.

Honestly.  Idk what we're going to do with the younger generations. In ways they are way over exposed and in other ways, they're super sheltered.  They live online,  not in the real world.  

The internet has changed the way that people interact with other people.  And not in a good way.  Children don't learn by experience anymore. So when they go out into the real world,  they do stupid shyt like this. 

And also society as a whole has lost their ability to feel empathy or compassion for anyone or anything that doesn't directly effect them.  I'm not a particularly religious person.  I'm agnostic.  But I find a creepy irony in the fact that a 2,000 year old book (the Bible) says that in the end times people will be judgemental and unforgiving.  It's not a compliment to our current culture and is pretty spot on.  

Before the internet age, kids doing dumb shyt was to be expected.  A part of life. And part of learning.  

There's an old saying, don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.  I think that applies well here. What this girl has done is deplorable.  But with very very few exceptions,  no child is beyond redemption. And yes. I'm going to call her a child. She isn't old enough to buy a drink in a bar or buy a gun in California.  Because she's not grown yet. Her brain is still developing.  

If you're hell bent on having someone to direct your ire to.. How about you direct it to the society that has created this mess.

My generation was disciplined and we learned to respect our elders. We learned to respect our communities.  We didn't need nor have almost as many juvenile detention centers as adult prisons.  

Think about this logically.  Yeah this girl did wrong.  But was she truly ever taught any better? 

I don't believe that she deserves 20 years in prison.  Prisons turn people who made a dumb decision into real criminals.  I think that she needs to be banned from working in this field which I feel she wasn't old enough to be doing in the first place.  And a lot of community service and probation. Prison would just teach her how to be a criminal.  It takes a village to raise a child. But what if this girls village was too busy to raise her?

Content: Not only is this sexual battery against a disabled person, but it is also a HIPAA violation since she released images of the patients.  Since this was a willful HIPAA violation, it would be considered either tier 3 or 4.  Tier 3 has fines between $10k & $50 per violation.  Tier 4 has fines between $50k & $1.5M.  It all depends on how long she left the videos up.  If they were up for more than 30 days, then it is a tier 4.  This is on the Federal level.  State Attorneys can also issue fines for HIPAA violation.  The patients or their families would need to file the complaints for either to happen though.

Content:
I used to work in clinical governance and we had a student nurse at the hospital bragging on TikTok about being allowed in on a surgery and holding the patient's heart. She had recorded TikToks of herself in patient's rooms, in sensitive clinical and non-clinical areas aaaaaand even described how she'd "intervened" when an actual nurse was assisting a patient. Which had to have a separate investigation due to the allegations. These were found to be false. 

She not only lost her job at the hospital, but also her license and place at university. She is banned from the nursing register for life and blacklisted from the university (meaning she can't study anything there). She also will have a stain that will show up with a DBS check. All that for some TikTok clout. She tried to delete them thinking we couldn't do anything without the evidence, but I'd downloaded the whole lot. 

To top it all off, they also sent the hospital media team on a course to learn what is and isn't legal/appropriate to share on social media after the deputy of the team tried defending her to me saying "She's just really passionate about her job." 😂
